arrays_strings.overview: Arrays & Strings power 40%+ of screening rounds. Master two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums, and hash maps first — they unlock most easy-medium problems.

cards.title: Two Pointers — Full Guide
cards.body:
**When:** sorted array, pair/triplet sum, palindrome, container area.

**Template:** left=0, right=n-1; move based on comparison to target.

**3Sum:** sort → fix i → two-pointer on [i+1..n-1]; skip duplicates.

**Memory:** *Sorted + pair = squeeze from both ends.*

cards.title: Sliding Window — Variable & Fixed
cards.body:
**Invariant:** window always valid (or track invalid count).

1. Expand `end`
2. While invalid → shrink `start`
3. Update answer when valid

**Fixed k:** sum first k, slide by add right / remove left.

**Trap:** updating max before shrinking when problem requires valid window only.

cards.title: Kadane's Maximum Subarray
cards.body:
At each index: **start fresh or extend?**
`cur = max(nums[i], cur + nums[i])`

**Hiking trail:** negative cumulative baggage → drop it.

Follow-up: return actual subarray → track tempStart/start/end.

Time O(n), Space O(1).

cards.title: Prefix Sum + HashMap
cards.body:
Identity: `sum(i..j) = prefix[j] - prefix[i-1]`

Seeking subarray sum = K → at each prefix `p`, count how many prior prefixes equal `p - K`.

**Seed `{0:1}`** — empty prefix enables subarray starting at 0.

**Active recall:** Why seed 0? → subarrays from index 0.

cards.title: HashMap Frequency Patterns
cards.body:
Anagrams: count chars, compare maps or single map with +/-.
Top-K frequent: heap or bucket sort by frequency.

**Mnemonic:** *Count → Compare → Combine*

cards.title: Difference Arrays
cards.body:
Range update [l,r] += val in O(1): `diff[l]+=val`, `diff[r+1]-=val`. Prefix sum diff → final array.

Use when many range increments on static base.

trees_graphs.overview: Highest-weight DSA area. Order: traversals → BST → BFS/DFS → topo → Union-Find → shortest path.

cards.title: Tree Traversals Deep Dive
cards.body:
**Inorder (LNR):** BST → sorted order.
**Preorder (NLR):** serialize/copy tree.
**Postorder (LRN):** delete tree, evaluate expressions.

Iterative inorder: stack, go left, pop, go right.

Space O(h) recursion, O(n) worst skewed tree.

cards.title: BST Operations & Validation
cards.body:
Search/insert/delete O(h). Balanced → O(log n).

Validate BST: pass (min,max) range per node — not just left<root<right locally.

**Recall:** Why range check? → local check misses cross-subtree violations.

cards.title: BFS vs DFS — Decision Tree
cards.body:
**BFS:** unweighted shortest path, level-order, multi-source spread.
**DFS:** connectivity, cycles, topo sort, path enumeration.

**Mnemonic:** *Breadth = shortest steps, Depth = explore fully.*

cards.title: Topological Sort & Cycle Detection
cards.body:
**Kahn (BFS):** in-degree 0 queue → reduce neighbors.
**DFS:** visiting/visited; edge to visiting = cycle.

Apps: build order, course schedule, dependency DAG.

cards.title: Union-Find (DSU)
cards.body:
**FIND** root with path compression.
**UNION** by rank/size.

Nearly O(1) amortized.

**Triggers:** connected components, redundant edge, accounts merge, Kruskal MST.

**Mnemonic:** FURC — Find, Union, Rank, Compress.

cards.title: Shortest Path Algorithms
cards.body:
| Algo | When |
|---|---|
| BFS | Unweighted |
| Dijkstra | Non-negative weights |
| Bellman-Ford | Negative edges, detect cycle |
| Floyd-Warshall | All pairs (small n) |

**Recall:** Why Dijkstra fails with negative edge? → greedy assumption broken.

dp.overview: DP = optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems. Define state before transitions.

cards.title: DP Problem-Solving Framework
cards.body:
1. Define state (what does `dp[i]` mean?)
2. Write recurrence
3. Base cases
4. Order of computation
5. Space optimize if only prior row/states needed

**Feynman:** Explain Fibonacci DP to a junior without saying 'memoization' first.

cards.title: 1D DP — Climbing Stairs & House Robber
cards.body:
Stairs: `dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2]` → optimize to two vars.

Robber: `dp[i]=max(dp[i-1], nums[i]+dp[i-2])` — can't take adjacent.

**Mnemonic:** SKIP or TAKE-SKIP-ONE.

cards.title: 2D DP — Grid Paths & LCS
cards.body:
Grid: `dp[r][c]=dp[r-1][c]+dp[r][c-1]` with obstacles.
LCS: match → diag+1; else max(up,left).

Draw table in interview — buys thinking time.

cards.title: Knapsack Family
cards.body:
**0/1:** loop capacity backwards (each item once).
**Unbounded:** loop forwards (reuse allowed).
**Subset sum:** can we reach target T?

**Recall:** Why backwards for 0/1? → prevents using same item twice in one pass.

cards.title: State Machine DP
cards.body:
When behavior depends on mode: hold/sold/cooldown, buy/sell with fee.

Steps: list modes → transitions → DP over (index, mode).

Classic: Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock with cooldown.

**Principal:** State machine DP is how you extend greedy stock problems.

heaps.overview: Heaps = O(log n) insert/extract for streaming and Top-K.

cards.title: Top-K Elements
cards.body:
K **largest** → min-heap size K (root = weakest winner).
K **smallest** → max-heap size K.

Time O(n log k) vs sort O(n log n).

cards.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
cards.body:
Min-heap of list heads; pop smallest, push next from that list.
Alt: divide-and-conquer merge pairs.

cards.title: Median from Data Stream
cards.body:
Max-heap (lower half) + min-heap (upper half). Keep sizes balanced (diff ≤ 1).

Median = top of max-heap or average of both tops.

bit_manipulation.overview: Lower frequency but fast wins. XOR and bitmasks.

cards.title: XOR & Bit Counting
cards.body:
`a^a=0`, `a^0=a` → single number among pairs.
Brian Kernighan: `n&(n-1)` clears lowest set bit.

Bitmask DP: iterate subsets of mask.

oop_solid.overview: SOLID + composition is the LLD backbone. Principal bar = explain Liskov failures.

cards.title: LLD Interview Framework (9 Steps)
cards.body:
1. **CLARIFY** scope
2. **NOUNS** → entities
3. **VERBS** → methods
4. **RELATIONSHIPS** is-a vs has-a
5. **PATTERNS** from requirements
6. **SKELETON** interfaces first
7. **CODE** narrate aloud
8. **TEST** happy + edge + transitions
9. **EXTEND** what changes if requirement shifts

cards.title: SOLID — Principal Depth
cards.body:
**S:** one reason to change (billing vs email).
**O:** extend via new classes.
**L:** subclass substitutable — Square/Rectangle fail.
**I:** small interfaces, no fat contracts.
**D:** depend on abstractions; Spring DI.

**Feynman:** Explain Liskov using Square extends Rectangle.

cards.title: Composition Over Inheritance
cards.body:
Wrong: `GoldMember extends Member` — tier can't change at runtime.
Right: `Member has-a Membership has-a Plan`.

Rule: inheritance only if is-a is fixed for object's lifetime.

cards.title: Interface Segregation in Practice
cards.body:
Split `Worker` into `Workable`, `Eatable` — Robot implements only Workable.
Fat interface → empty methods → hidden coupling.

design_patterns.overview: Name patterns from requirements, never force them.

cards.title: Pattern Trigger Table
cards.body:
| Signal | Pattern |
|---|---|
| Behavior varies by type | Strategy |
| Create by input type | Factory |
| One instance | Singleton (prefer DI) |
| Notify many on event | Observer |
| Lifecycle stages | State |
| Stack optional features | Decorator |
| Mismatched API | Adapter |
| Many optional ctor params | Builder |

cards.title: Strategy Pattern
cards.body:
Encapsulate varying algorithm. Gym: `MembershipPlan.getMonthlyFee()` per tier.
Adding tier = new class, zero edits to billing loop.

cards.title: Factory Pattern
cards.body:
Centralize creation: `PlanFactory.create(Tier.GOLD)`.
Hides concrete types from callers.

cards.title: Observer Pattern
cards.body: Subject notifies observers on state change. Membership expiry → billing, email, analytics.

cards.title: Decorator vs Adapter
cards.body:
**Decorator:** add behavior, same interface (logging around PaymentService).
**Adapter:** translate incompatible interface (LegacyGateway → PaymentGateway).

**Mnemonic:** Adapter=Translate, Decorator=Stack.

cards.title: Singleton — Principal Stance
cards.body:
Thread-safe: enum singleton, holder idiom.
**Interview answer:** prefer DI; singleton hurts testing and multi-tenant isolation.

classic_lld.overview: Entity model + invariants + patterns. Clarify before coding.

cards.title: Parking Lot — Full Model
cards.body:
**Entities:** ParkingLot, Floor, SpotType, Spot, Vehicle, Ticket, Payment.
**Flows:** enter → assign spot → ticket; exit → pay → free spot.
**Patterns:** Strategy (pricing), Factory (spot assignment).
**Concurrency:** lock spot row / optimistic version on allocate.

cards.title: Elevator System
cards.body:
**Entities:** Building, Elevator, Request(floor, direction), Controller.
**State:** Idle, MovingUp, MovingDown, DoorOpen.
**Dispatch:** SCAN vs nearest-car.
**Concurrency:** request queue per elevator.

cards.title: BookMyShow / Seat Booking
cards.body:
**Entities:** Movie, Show, Screen, Seat, Booking, Payment.
**Critical:** seat hold with TTL → payment → confirm.
**Consistency:** pessimistic row lock OR Redis hold key OR conditional update.
**Failure:** double-book if no hold TTL or idempotent confirm.

cards.title: Vending Machine
cards.body:
**State pattern:** Idle → HasMoney → Dispensing → Idle.
**Entities:** Inventory, CoinStore, ProductSlot.
**Edge:** insufficient change, empty slot, cancel → refund.

cards.title: Splitwise / Expense Sharing
cards.body:
**Entities:** User, Group, Expense, SplitStrategy (equal/exact/%).
**Graph:** balances between users; simplify debts (min cash flow).
**Pattern:** Strategy for split types.

cards.title: LRU / LFU Cache
cards.body:
**LRU:** HashMap + doubly linked list OR access-order LinkedHashMap.
**LFU:** freq buckets + doubly linked lists.

Say O(1) get/put. Distributed follow-up: eviction broadcast, TTL, near-cache.

concurrency_lld.overview: Thread-safety, backpressure, rate limits — common in Principal LLD.

cards.title: Rate Limiter — Token Bucket
cards.body:
Refill tokens at rate r; capacity B allows bursts.
`tryAcquire()` synchronized for single JVM.

**Distributed:** Redis + Lua atomic script.
**Algorithms:** token bucket, sliding window log, sliding counter (approx).

cards.title: Producer-Consumer
cards.body:
`BlockingQueue`: put blocks when full, take when empty.
Decouples producer rate from consumer.

Backpressure = bounded queue.

cards.title: Concurrent Collections
cards.body:
Default `ConcurrentHashMap` over synchronized HashMap.
`CopyOnWriteArrayList` for read-heavy.
`ArrayDeque` for stack/queue — not LinkedList.

fundamentals.overview: CAP/PACELC, caching, LB, DB scaling — foundation for every HLD.

cards.title: CAP & PACELC
cards.body:
**CAP:** under Partition, choose Availability or Consistency.
**PACELC:** else (normal ops), choose Latency or Consistency.

Banking → CP. Social likes → AP.

**Consistency models:** strong, causal, eventual — name them in interviews.

cards.title: Caching — Patterns & Failures
cards.body:
| Pattern | Pros | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| Cache-aside | Simple | Stampede on hot key |
| Write-through | Consistent cache | Write latency |
| Write-behind | Fast writes | Loss on crash |

Mitigate stampede: singleflight, soft+hard TTL, jitter.

cards.title: Load Balancing
cards.body:
L4 (TCP/NLB) vs L7 (HTTP/ALB).
Algos: round-robin, least connections, consistent hashing (caches).

Sticky sessions — avoid if possible; externalize session to Redis.

cards.title: Sharding & Replication
cards.body:
Shard key dominates — hot partition = bottleneck.
Replication: leader-follower for reads; quorum for writes.

**Principal line:** shard by tenant_id for isolation, user_id for even load.

messaging.overview: Kafka + delivery semantics + outbox — Principal must-know.

cards.title: Kafka Internals
cards.body:
Topic → partitions (parallelism unit) → offsets.
Ordering **within** partition only. Key = partition routing.
Consumer group: 1 consumer per partition max.

Lag = consumer SLO metric.

cards.title: Delivery Semantics
cards.body:
**At-most-once:** commit offset before process.
**At-least-once:** process then commit; need idempotency.
**Exactly-once:** transactional + idempotent sink (expensive).

**Mnemonic:** AMAL — At-most, At-least, idempotent for At-least.

cards.title: Outbox Pattern & DLQ
cards.body:
**Outbox:** same DB txn writes business row + outbox event; relay publishes.
**DLQ:** poison messages after N retries.
**Compaction:** Kafka keeps latest value per key.

classic_hld.overview: Classic designs — always include capacity math and failure modes.

cards.title: URL Shortener
cards.body:
Write: hash → base62 → store (user_id, long_url).
Read: cache (Redis) → DB. 301 vs 302.
Scale: read-heavy; CDN; shard by hash prefix.

Capacity: 62^7 ≈ 3.5T URLs.

cards.title: News Feed / Timeline
cards.body:
**Push:** fanout on write (good for few followers).
**Pull:** fanout on read (good for many followers).
**Hybrid:** push celebrities, pull normal users.

Storage: per-user timeline = sorted post IDs.

cards.title: Chat System
cards.body:
WebSocket gateway; message queue for persistence.
Per-conversation sequence for ordering.
Presence: heartbeat + Redis set.
Offline: store-and-forward, sync on reconnect.

cards.title: Video Streaming (YouTube)
cards.body:
Upload → transcode ladder (HLS/DASH) → S3 → CDN.
Metadata DB separate from blob store.
ABR: client picks bitrate by bandwidth.

**Bottlenecks:** egress cost, transcode farm, hot viral video.

cards.title: Distributed Rate Limiter
cards.body:
Gateway (API GW) or sidecar (Envoy) or Redis cluster.
Sliding window counter in Redis (INCR + EXPIRE).

Tradeoff: accuracy vs memory vs cross-region sync.

scalability.overview: Resilience patterns and service topology tradeoffs.

cards.title: Horizontal vs Vertical
cards.body:
Vertical: bigger box, ceiling fast.
Horizontal: more nodes — needs stateless app, LB, external state.

Stateless + external session = scale app tier linearly.

cards.title: Microservices vs Monolith
cards.body:
Start modular monolith unless team/deploy independence forces split.
Microservices cost: network, observability, distributed transactions.

**Principal:** justify split with organizational or scale constraint.

cards.title: Circuit Breaker & Bulkhead
cards.body:
CB: Closed → Open (fail fast) → Half-open (probe).
Bulkhead: separate thread pools per dependency.

Prevents cascade when dependency slow/failing.

jvm.overview: JVM memory, GC, JIT — senior Java screens.

cards.title: JVM Memory Model
cards.body:
**Heap:** Eden → Survivor → Old gen.
**Stack:** per-thread frames.
**Metaspace:** class metadata (Java 8+).

Short-lived objects die in young GC (generational hypothesis).

cards.title: GC Algorithms
cards.body:
**G1:** region-based, pause targets.
**ZGC/Shenandoah:** sub-ms pauses, large heaps.

Minor GC (young), Major GC (old), STW events.

**Recall:** Why first request after deploy slow? → cold JIT + caches.

cards.title: JIT Compilation
cards.body:
Interpreted → C1 (quick) → C2 (aggressive opt) for hot methods.
Deoptimization if assumptions break.

`-XX:+PrintCompilation` for debugging (mention awareness).

spring.overview: Spring Boot DI, transactions, auto-config — full-stack screens.

cards.title: Auto-Configuration
cards.body:
Classpath + `@ConditionalOn*` wires defaults.
Override with explicit `@Bean`.

`spring.factories` / `AutoConfiguration.imports` register auto-config classes.

cards.title: Bean Lifecycle & DI
cards.body:
Constructor injection preferred (immutable, testable).
Scopes: singleton (default), prototype, request, session.

Circular deps: redesign or `@Lazy` (smell).

cards.title: Transaction Management Traps
cards.body:
`@Transactional` via proxy — self-invocation bypasses it.
Rollback: RuntimeException yes, checked no (by default).

`REQUIRES_NEW` for independent side-effect txn.

Emit events? → outbox, not naive afterCommit only.

cards.title: Raft Consensus
cards.body:
Leader election → log replication → commit on majority.
State machine applies committed entries.

Used: etcd, Consul. Simpler mental model than Paxos.

cards.title: Distributed Locks & Fencing
cards.body:
Redis `SET NX PX` alone is insufficient.
Problem: lock holder GC-pauses past TTL → two holders.

**Fencing token:** monotonic token per lock; storage rejects stale writes.

Prefer etcd/ZooKeeper lease or DB lease with fencing.

cards.title: Idempotency Patterns
cards.body:
Client idempotency key → store response in Redis/DB.
Consumer: dedupe table by event_id.

Goal: exactly-once **effect** without exactly-once delivery.

aws_platform.overview: Map abstract HLD to AWS — your stack (Java/Spring on AWS). Principal interviews expect named services after the design.

cards.title: AWS Service Mapping for HLD
cards.body:
| Need | AWS Service |
|---|---|
| L7 load balance | ALB |
| Async buffer | SQS |
| Pub/sub fan-out | SNS |
| Event routing | EventBridge |
| Hot cache / sessions | ElastiCache Redis |
| Object/video storage | S3 + CloudFront |
| Key-value at scale | DynamoDB |
| Relational | RDS/Aurora |
| Serverless compute | Lambda |
| Containers | ECS/EKS |
| API edge | API Gateway |

cards.title: Loosely Coupled AWS Design
cards.body:
Stateless compute (ECS/Lambda) + external state (DynamoDB, Redis, S3).
SQS decouples spikes. SNS/EventBridge for fan-out.

Failure isolation: one slow queue consumer doesn't block API.

cards.title: DynamoDB Design Notes
cards.body:
Partition key = scalability unit. Avoid hot keys.
On-demand vs provisioned. GSIs for alternate access patterns.
Streams + Lambda for CDC.

star_stories.overview: 5 STAR stories ≤2 min each with technical depth and metrics.

cards.title: STAR for Principal
cards.body:
**S** 1 sentence context
**T** your ownership scope
**A** technical decisions YOU made
**R** quantified outcome

Principal: Action must show tradeoff analysis + influence without authority.

cards.title: Conflict Resolution Story
cards.body:
Technical disagreement → data/metrics → prototype or spike → decision.
Avoid blame. Show listening.

cards.title: Failure & Learning Story
cards.body:
Own the miss. What signal you missed. Process change after.
Principal: systemic fix, not heroics.

cards.title: Delivering Under Pressure
cards.body:
Scope cut, risk communication, incremental ship.
Metrics: uptime, latency, revenue protected.

principal_topics.overview: ADR, hiring, tech vision — Staff/Principal loop differentiators.

cards.title: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
cards.body:
1. Context & constraints
2. Options (≥2)
3. Tradeoffs table
4. Decision + rationale
5. Consequences
6. Revisit triggers

**Drill:** Write one real ADR from memory weekly.

cards.title: Team Scaling & Hiring
cards.body:
Define interview signal per level. Bar-raiser mindset.
Onboarding: ownership boundaries, first 30/60/90.

**Recall:** What distinguishes Staff from Senior in your rubric?

cards.title: Technical Vision & Roadmap
cards.body:
Current state → constraints → 12-month bets → risks → metrics.
Tie to business outcome, not technology for its own sake.

cards.title: Questions to Ask Principal Interviewer
cards.body:
- Success in first 90 days at this level?
- Biggest platform/architecture pain?
- How are ADRs / tech strategy decided?
- On-call model and quality bar?
- What does 'Principal impact' look like here?

cards.title: Company Research Checklist
cards.body:
Recent earnings/blog engineering posts. Product bets. Competitors.
Map your stories to their domain (fintech, ads, logistics, etc.).

microLessons.title: Karat Communication Script
microLessons.body:
1. Restate 2. Clarify 3. Brute force aloud 4. State optimization 5. Narrate while coding 6. Complexity unprompted 7. Test sample input

Narrated partial > silent perfect.

microLessons.title: Extension Question Chains
microLessons.body:
Part 1 working + Part 2 attempted > polished Part 1 only.
Two Sum → 3Sum → k Sum. LRU → thread-safe → distributed.

microLessons.title: DSA Pattern Triggers
microLessons.body:
Sorted+O(log n)→Binary Search
Pair sum→Two Ptr/HashMap
Subarray→Sliding Window
K largest→Min-heap size K
Intervals→Sort+Greedy
Cycle→DFS/Floyd

microLessons.title: Feynman Technique
microLessons.body: Explain topic to a junior in plain language. Stalls = gaps to study. Record 3-min voice note after each HLD topic.

microLessons.title: Active Recall Rule
microLessons.body: Never re-read notes first. Question on card → answer from memory → check. Failed? Mark Needs Revision in app.

microLessons.title: LLD Recovery Script
microLessons.body: Never silent >10s. 'Let me list entities...' Sketch nouns. Simplest pattern. 'With more time I'd add X.'

microLessons.title: Fencing Token Recall
microLessons.body: Lock TTL + GC pause = two holders. Fencing token: storage rejects writes with stale token. Always mention in distributed lock answers.

microLessons.title: 90-Day Daily Rhythm
microLessons.body:
Mon DSA · Tue LLD · Wed DSA timed · Thu HLD · Fri LLD/behavioral · Sat mock · Sun revision+plan.
Use Today Focus + Revision every day.
